newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo Metal has positive Alaska gold drill result.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo Metal has positive Alaska gold drill result.

text.p: Sumitomo Metal Mining Co said on Thursday that a Japanese agency reported promising gold drilling results at a site in Alaska held by one of the company's U.S. subsidiaries.

The Metal Mining Agency of Japan said it discovered at the Stone Boy region near Fairbanks an area of significant gold mineralisation covering at least 450 metres by 250 metres, indicating a strong possibility of a promising gold deposit.
Mineral rights to the site are owned by Sumitomo Metal Mining Arizona Inc, which is 75 percent owned by Sumitomo Metal Mining and 25 percent by trade house Sumitomo Corp.

A Sumitomo Metal spokesman said more drilling was scheduled for June through September of this year on a scale about double the size of the drilling already conducted, although it was too early in the exploration process to determine whether or when a feasibility study might be carried out.
"We are very pleased that the Metal Mining Agency of Japan's drilling has confirmed a significant gold vein," Sumitomo Metal senior managing director Koichi Sudo said in a statement.
The agency reported that a 10.4-metre core sample graded 31.8 grams per tonne of gold and that a 1.0-metre sample graded 322.9 grams per tonne.
The site was near Amax Gold Inc's Fort Knox gold mine, which is expected to produce at a rate of 350,000 ounces per year when it reaches full production around mid-year.
The agency also said in a statement that Alaska had in recent years adopted favourable tax measures for the mining industry and was actively seeking to promote the development of its mining sector.
Sumitomo Metal Mining is Japan's leading gold miner and holds a minority stake in copper mines in Arizona and Chile through its Arizona unit.
The Metal Mining Agency of Japan supports overseas mining exploration activities with government funding.
